findings.consequence: Any caller holding an active receipt and outcome can directly construct unlimited same-kind leases, choose an arbitrary payload, consume each once, and bypass TickAdmissionReceiptV1._issued_kinds. This defeats the sole-mint, exact-payload, and one-consumer authority boundary.
findings.evidence: An accelerator-hidden adversarial probe directly constructed two target_red leases and one physical_view lease carrying a caller-authored visible-cell mapping; every consume succeeded and the runtime remained committable.
findings.required_correction: Make lease creation require a receipt-owned, unforgeable exact mint capability; bind kind to an exact payload object/type and issued registry entry; reject direct/reconstructed leases terminally before payload return.

findings.consequence: Tick zero need not start from the ResetReceiptV1 zero state, reset/session identities can be reused across runtimes, and a caller can author the physical/configuration revisions and commitment hashes from which view/target leases are minted. The G4 call likewise accepts an independently reconstructed candidate batch rather than an exact receipt-bound CandidateSetV3 object.
findings.evidence: An adversarial probe constructed two runtimes with identical reset/session IDs and nonzero initial physical/configuration revisions, admitted and committed both. The public admit_tick signature accepts scalar revisions and six caller hashes; run_g4_value_head_once accepts a caller-supplied FrozenCandidateFeatureBatchV1.
findings.required_correction: Bind runtime construction to one exact fresh ResetReceiptV1/capability with canonical zero owner state; remove nonzero tick-zero initialization; admit only exact single-use physical/projection producer receipts; bind G4 scoring to the exact receipt-minted immutable candidate object shared with the baseline.

findings.consequence: A hash-contiguous trace can skip physical, configuration, view, four target, and claim-journal revisions between ticks, start from nonzero revisions after a zero reset, and publish unrelated final owner revisions while still validating.
findings.evidence: An adversarial two-tick ControllerTraceV1 with tick-one pre-revisions 100/200/300 and target pre-revisions 400/500/600/700 after tick zero post-revisions of one, plus all-zero final_owner_revisions, was accepted.
findings.required_correction: Derive the first pre-state from ResetReceiptV1, require every typed pre-revision/content commitment to equal the prior committed post-state, and derive/validate every final_owner_revisions row from the final tick or reset state.

findings.consequence: The returned four-color head object remains mutable before admission. Admission hashes its current bytes rather than validating the exact output produced by the one counted call, so invalid probability and quality domains can become authoritative target lease payloads.
findings.evidence: An adversarial probe changed every presence_probability to 2.0 and quality to -3.0 after the head call; admit_tick accepted them and a canonical red target lease returned those invalid values.
findings.required_correction: Freeze and content-bind a detached output snapshot immediately inside the counted head call, retain tensor versions/content, revalidate all output domains at admission, and reject any pre-admission mutation instead of rebinding it.

findings.consequence: The ledger cannot append the actual duplicate attempt that denied_duplicate is meant to record, yet it accepts denied_duplicate as the first open and accepts other denied dispositions without disposition-specific evidence. The append-only chain therefore does not prove the claimed open decision.
findings.evidence: A duplicate tuple with denied_duplicate was rejected by the global duplicate-row rule, while an empty ledger accepted a first row marked denied_duplicate with equal expected/actual hashes.
findings.required_correction: Represent every attempted open as a chained event, including the terminal duplicate attempt, and validate each access_disposition against exact prior rows, hashes, actor, phase, path, and no-follow evidence.

findings.consequence: The closed trace admits semantically impossible branch combinations, so action-source accounting cannot prove which mandatory target, learned-G4, stop, or fault path produced the command.
findings.evidence: An exploration tick with one G4 call, complete G4 bindings, and action_source target_router was accepted by NavigationTickRecordV1 and ControllerTraceV1.
findings.required_correction: Close each decision union over action_source, fault/stall state, target/G4 fields, selected row/path/yaw, command source, and claim fields; reject every cross-branch combination before hashing.
